experiences.name: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne
experiences.description: Embark on a traditional Maldivian wooden boat (dhoni) decorated with flowers and candles for a private sunset cruise. Sip champagne while watching the Indian Ocean sky transform into shades of gold and pink. Perfect for honeymooners seeking an intimate and unforgettable romantic experience on the water.
experiences.location: North Malé Atoll, near Hulhumalé lagoon

experiences.name: House Reef Snorkeling Safari with Marine Biologist
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant coral gardens and teeming marine life of a pristine house reef guided by a certified marine biologist. Encounter sea turtles, reef sharks, manta rays, and hundreds of tropical fish species. Snorkeling equipment is provided, and the guide offers fascinating insights into the Maldivian ecosystem throughout the experience.
experiences.location: South Ari Atoll, near Rangali Island

experiences.name: Underwater Spa Treatment
experiences.description: Indulge in a signature couples massage inside a breathtaking glass-walled underwater spa suite surrounded by the turquoise ocean and tropical fish. This ultra-luxurious experience combines therapeutic relaxation with the mesmerizing beauty of the Maldivian sea, making it an iconic and deeply romantic honeymoon memory.
experiences.location: Conrad Maldives Rangali Island, Alif Dhaal Atoll

experiences.name: Maldivian Cooking Class and Beachside Dinner
experiences.description: Learn to prepare authentic Maldivian dishes such as mas huni (tuna and coconut salad), garudhiya fish soup, and coconut-infused curries from a local chef. After the class, enjoy your freshly prepared meal at a candlelit table set directly on the white sand beach under a canopy of stars — a truly magical cultural and culinary experience for couples.

experiences.name: Bioluminescent Night Snorkeling Experience
experiences.description: Slip into the warm, dark waters of the Indian Ocean after sunset to witness the magical phenomenon of bioluminescence — glowing plankton that light up the sea like a constellation of stars beneath the surface. A guided and safe experience with expert instructors, this rare natural wonder is one of the most romantic and awe-inspiring activities available in the Maldives.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Maldives
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: North Malé Atoll, near Hulhumalé lagoon Boutique Stay
hotel.location: North Malé Atoll, near Hulhumalé lagoon

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, then take the affordable public ferry (around $1 USD) to Hulhumalé island. Check into your boutique stay near Hulhumalé lagoon, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the Hulhumalé beachfront to get oriented. The lagoon area offers calm, clear turquoise waters perfect for a first glimpse of Maldivian beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Hulhumalé Beach — one of the most accessible and beautiful free experiences in the Maldives. Explore the local streets around the guesthouse and pick up any essentials from a nearby convenience store.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or skip
meals.lunch: Grab a quick local bite at a café near the Hulhumalé ferry terminal — try short eats (hedhikaa) like bajiya (fish pastry) or gulha for under $3
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Maldivian restaurant in Hulhumalé such as Sala Thai or a local eatery serving mas riha (fish curry) with roshi (flatbread) for $5–8

day_by_day.notes: Public ferry from airport to Hulhumalé costs approx. $1 and runs frequently. Keep your passport handy for check-in. Exchange some USD to MVR (Maldivian Rufiyaa) at the airport for small local purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk along Hulhumalé lagoon beach — the water is incredibly calm and shallow here, ideal for a free swim or wade. Rent basic snorkel gear from a local dive shop near the beach (approx. $5–8/day) and explore the lagoon's coral patches just off the shore. Hulhumalé lagoon hosts small reef fish and occasional sea turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the short public ferry to Malé city (approx. $1, 15 minutes). Explore the capital on foot — visit the iconic Maldives Islamic Centre with its golden dome, the Old Friday Mosque (Hukuru Miskiy) built in 1658 from coral stone, and the nearby cemetery. Walk through the colorful local market area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Malé's waterfront promenade (Rasfannu) and browse the local fish market where fishermen bring in the daily catch. Head back to Hulhumalé on the evening ferry. Relax at the guesthouse.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at guesthouse or local café — try mas huni (tuna with coconut) with roshi, a classic Maldivian breakfast for $3–5
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Malé — visit the local eateries near the market for a plate of garudhiya (fish broth soup) with rice for $4–6
meals.dinner: Dinner at a budget restaurant in Hulhumalé — try Seagull Café or similar local spots for grilled fish with rice for $6–9

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting mosques in Malé — cover shoulders and knees. The Maldives Islamic Centre is closed to non-Muslims for prayer times but the exterior is stunning. Malé is very walkable — the entire island takes about 20 minutes to cross on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling session at Hulhumalé lagoon's reef edge. The outer reef drop-off near Hulhumalé hosts parrotfish, angelfish, and reef sharks. Bring your rented gear and go early (7–9am) when the water is calmest and marine life most active. This is completely free with your rented equipment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Book a budget snorkeling day trip through your guesthouse or a local operator — many offer shared group tours to nearby snorkeling spots in North Malé Atoll for $25–40 per person including boat transfer and snorkel gear. Popular spots include Banana Reef or HP Reef, both UNESCO-recognized dive sites with vibrant coral gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hulhumalé by late afternoon. Visit a local spa for a budget foot or back massage — some local wellness spots in Hulhumalé offer 30-minute sessions for $15–20. Enjoy a romantic evening walk along the lagoon as the sky turns pink.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at guesthouse — fresh tropical fruit, tea, and roshi
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks provided by the snorkeling tour operator, or bring your own from a local shop
meals.dinner: Romantic dinner for two at a beachfront restaurant in Hulhumalé — grilled lobster or snapper with coconut rice, budget $15–20 per couple

day_by_day.notes: Book snorkeling tours 1 day in advance through your guesthouse for the best group rates. Shared boats are significantly cheaper than private charters. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hulhumalé Artificial Beach on the north side of the island — a long, clean stretch of white sand that's less crowded in the mornings. Perfect for a romantic morning swim and sunbathing. The water here is shallow and crystal clear, great for snorkeling close to shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a speedboat day trip to a local uninhabited island (picnic island) — many budget operators offer this from Hulhumalé for $30–50 per person including boat, snorkeling stop, and beach time. Alternatively, visit Villingili island by ferry for a quieter local experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dolphin-watching cruise — one of the Maldives' most magical budget experiences. Shared group cruises depart from Hulhumalé marina and cost $20–30 per person. Spinner dolphins are commonly spotted in North Malé Atoll at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at guesthouse — egg dishes, fresh juice, and local bread
meals.lunch: Beachside BBQ lunch on the uninhabited island (usually included in day trip package) or bring a picnic
meals.dinner: Dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Hulhumalé for a romantic atmosphere — budget $10–15 per person for local Maldivian cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin cruises are best at sunset (around 5:30–7pm). Book in the morning as spots fill up. The uninhabited island trip is a quintessential Maldives experience even on a budget — negotiate group rates for better pricing.

day_by_day.morning: Slow, relaxing morning at the guesthouse — enjoy the lagoon view, have a leisurely breakfast, and read or spend quality romantic time together. Friday is the holy day in Maldives and many local businesses open later.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling at the Hulhumalé lagoon house reef — many boutique guesthouses near the lagoon have direct reef access. Spend 2–3 hours exploring coral formations, sea turtles, and tropical fish at your own pace. Free with rented gear.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hulhumalé's local art scene — the island has several murals and a growing creative community. Walk the streets to discover colorful street art. End the evening at a beachside café watching the stars over the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Full Maldivian breakfast at guesthouse — mas huni, roshi, and sweet black tea (sai)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café — tuna sandwich and fresh lime juice for $4–6
meals.dinner: Friday special dinner — many local restaurants offer grilled fish platters on Fridays. Try a set meal for $8–12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Friday prayers happen around noon — expect some businesses to close briefly. The Maldives is predominantly Muslim, so be respectful of local customs, especially on Fridays. Alcohol is not available on local islands.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Maafushi island — one of the Maldives' most popular budget travel destinations. Take a public ferry from Malé (approx. $5–8, 1.5–2 hours) or a speedboat (approx. $25–30, 45 minutes). Maafushi is in South Malé Atoll and offers excellent snorkeling, water sports, and a lively local island atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Maafushi's famous bikini beach (designated tourist beach), snorkel the house reef, and try water sports like kayaking or paddleboarding available for rent ($10–15/hour). Visit local dive shops for budget snorkeling excursions to nearby sandbanks.
day_by_day.evening: If doing a day trip, head back to Hulhumalé in the late afternoon. Alternatively, consider staying overnight in Maafushi at a budget guesthouse ($40–60/night) to save on transport costs and enjoy the island at night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at guesthouse before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Maafushi at a local restaurant — grilled fish with salad and rice for $7–10
meals.dinner: Dinner in Maafushi or back in Hulhumalé — fresh seafood platter for $10–15

day_by_day.notes: Public ferries run on fixed schedules — check timings in advance. Maafushi is one of the best budget destinations in Maldives with a wide range of water sports and excursions at competitive prices. Book water sports directly with local operators rather than through hotels for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip relaxation day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning at the guesthouse. Take a morning dip in the lagoon and practice snorkeling skills in the calm, shallow waters near the shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hulhumalé Central Park area and explore the island's newer residential zones — Hulhumalé is a fascinating reclaimed island with an interesting urban development story. Visit the local supermarket (STO or similar) to stock up on snacks, water, and supplies for the week ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic sunset picnic on the beach — buy fresh fruit, local snacks, and drinks from a supermarket and set up a simple picnic on the lagoon beach as the sun sets. A beautiful, free, and intimate experience.

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast at guesthouse
meals.lunch: Light lunch from a local takeaway — rice and curry combo for $4–6
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal if guesthouse has kitchen access, or dine at a local restaurant for $8–12 per couple

day_by_day.notes: This is a good day to do laundry, reorganize luggage, and plan the second half of the trip. Check with your guesthouse about any upcoming local events or festivals. Rest is important — pace yourself to enjoy the full trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkeling excursion to Banana Reef — one of the world's most famous snorkeling/diving sites, located in North Malé Atoll. Book a shared boat trip from Hulhumalé ($25–35 per person). The reef is known for its dramatic coral formations, moray eels, and schooling fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat excursion to a nearby sandbank — a tiny strip of white sand rising from the turquoise ocean, surrounded by nothing but sea. Spend an hour or two on this surreal natural wonder, perfect for romantic photos and swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hulhumalé by late afternoon. Visit a local spa for a couples' massage — some guesthouses offer in-house massage services for $30–50 per couple for a 60-minute session, much cheaper than resort spas.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the boat trip — toast, fruit, and tea
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the boat or at the sandbank — bring snacks and water from the guesthouse
meals.dinner: Special romantic dinner at the best local restaurant in Hulhumalé — fresh grilled red snapper with coconut curry for $12–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Banana Reef is best snorkeled in the morning when visibility is highest. Bring an underwater camera or waterproof phone case for amazing photos. The sandbank experience is one of the most iconic Maldivian memories you can have on a budget.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Malé city for a deeper cultural exploration. Take the early ferry and visit the National Museum of Maldives (entry approx. $3–5) to learn about the country's history, royal artifacts, and Buddhist heritage. The museum is housed in a historic building in Sultan Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Malé's vibrant local market (Malé Local Market) where vendors sell fresh tropical fruits, vegetables, and local handicrafts. Great for picking up affordable souvenirs like woven mats (thundu kunaa), lacquerwork, and local spices. Then walk to the Maldives Victory shipwreck viewpoint near the harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Malé's waterfront café scene — several cafés along the promenade offer coffee, fresh juices, and light bites with beautiful harbor views. Take the last ferry back to Hulhumalé and enjoy a quiet evening at the guesthouse.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at guesthouse before heading to Malé
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Maldivian eatery in Malé — hedhikaa (short eats) platter with tea for $3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at a popular local restaurant in Hulhumalé — try octopus curry or tuna steak for $8–12

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum is closed on Fridays. Bargaining is acceptable at the local market for handicrafts. Malé is very compact — most attractions are within a 10-minute walk of each other. The fish market near the harbor is most active in the late afternoon when fishing boats return.

day_by_day.morning: Water sports morning at Hulhumalé beach — rent a kayak ($10–15/hour) and paddle along the lagoon coastline for stunning views of the turquoise water. Alternatively, try stand-up paddleboarding, which is excellent for beginners in the calm lagoon waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Book a budget snorkeling trip to the famous Manta Point or a turtle cleaning station in North Malé Atoll (seasonal — check with local operators). Manta rays and sea turtles are frequently spotted in these areas. Shared group tours cost $30–45 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic beach bonfire evening (if permitted by guesthouse) or stargazing from the beach. The Maldives, with minimal light pollution over the ocean, offers spectacular stargazing. Bring a blanket and enjoy the night sky together.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at guesthouse — eggs, fruit, local bread, and tea
meals.lunch: Lunch on the snorkeling boat or at a beach shack — grilled corn and fresh coconut for $3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant — seafood pasta or grilled lobster (splurge slightly) for $15–20 per couple

day_by_day.notes: Manta ray sightings are seasonal (typically November–April in North Malé Atoll — March should be excellent). Always confirm with local operators the day before. Sea turtle encounters are more consistent year-round. This is a day for creating truly unforgettable honeymoon memories.

day_by_day.morning: Morning free time for personal relaxation — sleep in, enjoy the lagoon, or write postcards. Visit a local coffee shop in Hulhumalé for a slow breakfast with lagoon views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day boat excursion to a local fishing village island in North Malé Atoll — experience authentic Maldivian village life, see traditional boat building (dhoni building), and interact with local residents. Many budget operators offer this cultural experience for $20–30 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve romantic dinner — choose the best restaurant you've discovered during your stay for a special meal. Reflect on your trip highlights over good food and fresh coconut drinks.

meals.breakfast: Slow breakfast at a local café — iced coffee, fresh fruit bowl, and pastry for $5–7
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the cultural island tour — try local home-cooked food if offered by the tour
meals.dinner: Special dinner at your favorite restaurant from the trip — budget $20–25 for a memorable final proper dinner

day_by_day.notes: Consider buying final souvenirs today — local handicrafts, sarongs, or Maldivian spices make great gifts. Tip your guesthouse staff if you've had a great experience — it's greatly appreciated. Pack non-essentials tonight to make the final day easier.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning snorkeling session at Hulhumalé lagoon — one last swim in the crystal-clear waters. Take final photos of the lagoon, the guesthouse, and the beautiful surroundings to preserve the memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Light packing and checkout preparation. If checkout allows late check-out (ask guesthouse), relax on the beach for a few more hours. Otherwise, store luggage at the guesthouse and spend the afternoon at the beach or exploring any last spots you missed.
day_by_day.evening: Final sunset walk along Hulhumalé beach — watch the sky turn shades of orange, pink, and purple over the Indian Ocean. A perfect, free, and deeply romantic way to end the Maldives adventure.

meals.breakfast: Last breakfast at guesthouse — enjoy the full spread one final time
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local café in Hulhumalé — keep it light and easy
meals.dinner: Casual farewell dinner at a local restaurant — keep budget low as you'll need cash for airport expenses. $8–12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics with guesthouse — ask about the best ferry or transfer timing to the airport for your departure flight. The public ferry from Hulhumalé to the airport area is very affordable and convenient. Keep some MVR for last-minute purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. Wake up early, have a final light breakfast, and check out of the guesthouse. Take the public ferry or airport transfer to Velana International Airport. Arrive at the airport with at least 2–3 hours before your flight for international check-in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the airport duty-free shops for any last-minute gifts or souvenirs. Maldivian black coral jewelry, locally made chocolates, and branded Maldives souvenirs are popular picks. Relax in the departure lounge and reminisce about the incredible 13-day journey.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight, carrying memories of turquoise lagoons, vibrant coral reefs, romantic sunsets, and the warm hospitality of the Maldivian people.

meals.breakfast: Light early breakfast at guesthouse or grab a coffee and pastry near the ferry terminal
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport café or restaurant — budget $10–15
meals.dinner: Meal on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 13 days (per couple): Accommodation $600–900, Local transport $80–120, Snorkeling/excursions $300–450, Food $350–500, Souvenirs/misc $100–150. Total estimated budget: $1,430–$2,120 for two people — achievable for a budget Maldives honeymoon. Always confirm ferry schedules the night before departure.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and collect luggage. Take the arranged speedboat or ferry transfer to your boutique stay in North Malé Atoll near Hulhumalé lagoon. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the lagoon beach to soak in your first views of the turquoise waters. Enjoy a welcome drink and familiarize yourself with the property.
day_by_day.evening: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne — Board a traditional flower-and-candle-decorated Maldivian dhoni for a romantic sunset cruise. Sip champagne as the golden sun dips below the Indian Ocean horizon. Perfect honeymoon welcome experience.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at the airport or on arrival at the resort's welcome spread
meals.dinner: Dinner at the boutique stay's main restaurant — try grilled reef fish with coconut rice and a fresh tropical fruit platter. Mid-range set menu recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm speedboat/ferry transfer timing with the hotel in advance. Keep energy light on Day 1 to recover from travel. The sunset cruise is best booked for around 17:30–18:30.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely breakfast with lagoon views. After breakfast, head to the house reef for a guided House Reef Snorkeling Safari with a Marine Biologist. Discover vibrant coral gardens, reef sharks, sea turtles, and colorful tropical fish in the pristine waters just off the shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a relaxing lunch. Spend the early afternoon lounging by the pool or on the beach. Rent a paddleboard or kayak from the water sports center for a gentle self-guided lagoon exploration around Hulhumalé lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic beachside dinner under the stars at the resort's beach restaurant. Enjoy a candlelit table with the sound of gentle waves.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at the resort — fresh tropical fruits, eggs, pastries, and Maldivian short eats
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled fish wrap, fresh coconut water, and a tropical salad
meals.dinner: Beachside à la carte dinner — lobster thermidor or grilled mahi-mahi with sautéed vegetables and a bottle of house white wine

day_by_day.notes: The marine biologist snorkeling safari typically runs 2–2.5 hours. Bring reef-safe sunscreen. Book the safari the evening before to secure your preferred morning slot.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take a short boat trip to a nearby uninhabited sandbank. Enjoy a private picnic-style morning on the sandbank — swim in crystal-clear shallow waters, collect shells, and take stunning photos surrounded by nothing but ocean and sky.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort. Indulge in the Underwater Spa Treatment — a signature couples massage inside a breathtaking glass-walled underwater spa suite surrounded by marine life. A truly unforgettable honeymoon experience.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and unwind after the spa. Enjoy cocktails at the overwater bar as the evening sky turns pink and purple. Opt for an early dinner and a quiet evening on your private balcony.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit smoothie bowls, avocado toast, and freshly brewed Maldivian coffee at the resort café
meals.lunch: Sandbank picnic basket arranged by the resort — sandwiches, fruit skewers, fresh juice, and local snacks
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the resort's indoor restaurant — Maldivian curry with roshi flatbread and a refreshing mocktail or cocktail

day_by_day.notes: The sandbank excursion and underwater spa should be pre-booked. The spa session typically lasts 60–90 minutes per couple. Confirm sandbank availability with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Join a guided dolphin watching excursion by speedboat in the waters around North Malé Atoll. Spinner dolphins are frequently spotted in these waters, especially in the morning hours. Bring your camera for incredible wildlife moments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for lunch. Spend the afternoon taking a Maldivian Cooking Class — learn to prepare mas huni, garudhiya fish soup, and other authentic local dishes with a resort chef. A fun and interactive cultural experience perfect for couples.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Beachside Dinner component of the cooking class experience — sit down to a candlelit dinner on the beach featuring the dishes you prepared together, paired with fresh tropical juices or wine.

meals.breakfast: Light continental breakfast — croissants, jam, fresh orange juice, and yogurt with granola
meals.lunch: Resort restaurant lunch — tuna salad, fish curry soup, and steamed rice
meals.dinner: Beachside dinner featuring your own cooking class creations — mas huni, garudhiya, fresh roshi, and a sweet coconut dessert

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin watching excursions typically depart early morning (around 06:30–07:30) but can also run in the late afternoon. Confirm timing with the resort. The cooking class usually runs 2–3 hours including the dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning speedboat excursion to a nearby dive site for a snorkeling adventure at a famous coral reef in North Malé Atoll — sites like Banana Reef or HP Reef are accessible from this area. Swim alongside reef sharks, eagle rays, and dense schools of fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and enjoy a relaxed afternoon. Visit the resort spa for individual treatments — try a traditional Maldivian hot stone massage or a coconut oil body wrap. Alternatively, simply relax in a hammock with a book.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearby Hulhumalé area — take a short ferry or tuk-tuk ride to browse local shops, pick up Maldivian souvenirs, and enjoy the local atmosphere. Return to the resort for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full resort buffet breakfast — eggs Benedict, fresh tropical fruits, Maldivian hedhikaa (short eats), and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Light snack at the resort beach shack — fish spring rolls, coconut sambal, and a cold lime soda
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range local restaurant in Hulhumalé — try a traditional Maldivian fish curry with rice and rihaakuru (fish paste) for an authentic local dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Banana Reef and HP Reef require a 20–30 minute speedboat ride. Book through the resort's water sports desk. Hulhumalé is very accessible from North Malé Atoll and is great for budget-friendly local dining.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow, romantic morning — breakfast in bed or on your private balcony if the resort offers in-room dining. Spend the late morning swimming in the lagoon or snorkeling independently along the house reef at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join an afternoon big game fishing excursion. Try your hand at trolling for tuna, wahoo, or barracuda in the open waters of the Indian Ocean. Many resorts will arrange for your catch to be prepared for dinner.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special catch-of-the-day dinner — have the resort chef prepare your fish from the afternoon's fishing trip in your preferred style (grilled, curried, or ceviche). Dine on the beach with tiki torches and soft music.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast or balcony breakfast — fresh pastries, sliced tropical fruits, eggs, and Maldivian tea
meals.lunch: Light onboard snack during the fishing excursion — packed sandwiches, fruit, and cold drinks provided by the boat operator
meals.dinner: Catch-of-the-day beach dinner — grilled fish with garlic butter, roasted vegetables, coconut rice, and a dessert of panna cotta with mango coulis

day_by_day.notes: Fishing excursions typically run 3–4 hours in the afternoon. Confirm with the resort whether they can cook your catch. If fishing is not of interest, substitute with a sunset kayaking session or a guided nature walk.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint relaxation day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Spend the morning at the resort pool with cocktails, music, and sun loungers. Treat this as a true rest day — no excursions, just pure relaxation and romance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a couples' yoga or meditation session on the beach arranged through the resort. Many boutique properties in the Maldives offer wellness sessions. Follow with a refreshing dip in the lagoon and a nap in a beachside cabana.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent Night Snorkeling Experience — slip into the warm, dark Indian Ocean waters after sunset to witness the magical blue glow of bioluminescent plankton. A once-in-a-lifetime romantic experience perfect for honeymooners.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed late breakfast — smoothie bowls, eggs your way, fresh fruit platters, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch — club sandwich, sweet potato fries, and a fresh coconut to drink
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's overwater or beachside restaurant before the night snorkeling — grilled barracuda, vegetable stir-fry, and a shared dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Bioluminescent snorkeling is weather and season dependent — best confirmed with the resort on the day. The phenomenon is most visible on darker, calmer nights. March is generally an excellent month for this experience in the Maldives.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip by speedboat to Malé city — explore the historic Friday Mosque (Hukuru Miskiy), the National Museum, and the colorful fish market. Stroll through the busy streets and experience the authentic pulse of Maldivian urban life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Malé — visit local cafés and tea houses for traditional Maldivian short eats and sai (tea). Browse the local markets for handcrafted souvenirs, lacquerwork, and woven mats. Return to the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at the resort. Enjoy sundowners at the bar, then have a romantic dinner on the beach. Reflect on your week and enjoy the peaceful lagoon atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Quick resort breakfast before departure — toast, jam, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Maldivian café in Malé — try a traditional short eats spread (bajiya, gulha, keemia) with sai tea. Very affordable and authentic.
meals.dinner: Resort dinner — seafood pasta with a creamy bisque sauce, garlic bread, and a shared tiramisu for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Malé is a 20–30 minute speedboat ride from North Malé Atoll. Modest dress is recommended when visiting mosques. The fish market is most lively in the early morning, but afternoon visits still offer a great atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Second House Reef Snorkeling Safari with the Marine Biologist — revisit the house reef at a different time of day to spot nocturnal species emerging and different marine behavior. Early morning snorkeling often yields sightings of nurse sharks and sea turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on a private overwater bungalow day-use experience (if available through the resort or a nearby property). Enjoy direct lagoon access, sun loungers over the water, and a private butler service for a taste of ultimate luxury.
day_by_day.evening: Second Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne — celebrate your honeymoon midpoint with another magical sunset cruise. This time, request a personalized touch — a custom message in the sand on a nearby sandbank or a floating floral arrangement.

meals.breakfast: Full resort buffet — eggs, pastries, tropical fruits, yogurt, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Overwater bungalow day-use lunch — fresh seafood platter, tropical salad, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort's signature restaurant — tasting menu with wine pairing (splurge-worthy mid-trip treat). Expect dishes like seared tuna tataki, lobster bisque, and a chocolate fondant dessert.

day_by_day.notes: The overwater day-use experience may require advance booking and an additional fee. Check with the concierge. This is a great way to experience overwater living without upgrading your room category.

day_by_day.morning: Morning free — sleep in or enjoy a sunrise walk on the beach. Collect sea glass, watch the fishermen return with their morning catch, and breathe in the fresh ocean air. A perfect slow morning for two.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a guided manta ray or whale shark snorkeling excursion (seasonal — March is within the transition season; check availability with the resort). These gentle giants frequent the atolls around North Malé and offer a breathtaking snorkeling experience.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Maldivian cultural show — bodu beru drumming and dance performance, sometimes arranged by boutique resorts or accessible via a short trip to a nearby local island. Immerse yourself in the vibrant local culture.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed breakfast at the resort café — banana pancakes, fresh fruit, and Maldivian tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch before the excursion — fish tacos, green salad, and fresh lime juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local island restaurant (if attending the cultural show off-property) — traditional Maldivian rice and curry spread with coconut sambal and papadum

day_by_day.notes: Manta ray and whale shark sightings are not guaranteed but are common in this region during March. The resort's dive center will have the latest information on sighting locations. Cultural shows are often free or low-cost to attend.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a morning of water sports — try windsurfing, wakeboarding, or jet skiing through the resort's water sports center. Alternatively, rent a catamaran for a self-guided morning sail across the lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Underwater Spa Treatment (second session) — treat yourselves to another couples massage in the underwater spa. This time, opt for a different treatment — perhaps an aromatherapy session or a deep tissue massage with Maldivian herbal oils.
day_by_day.evening: Special honeymoon dinner setup — request the resort to arrange a private dining experience on the beach with lanterns, flower petals, a personalized menu, and a dedicated server. Many boutique resorts offer this as a complimentary or affordable add-on for honeymooners.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — fresh pastries, tropical fruit bowl, eggs, and freshly brewed coffee delivered to your room
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch — grilled chicken skewers, hummus with pita, and a refreshing watermelon juice
meals.dinner: Private beach honeymoon dinner — five-course set menu: amuse-bouche, prawn cocktail, cream of vegetable soup, pan-seared seabass, and a romantic dessert platter with 'Just Married' chocolate inscription

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private honeymoon dinner at least 2 days in advance with the resort concierge. Mention any dietary preferences or allergies. This is the perfect penultimate evening splurge before winding down the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — start with a sunrise snorkeling session independently on the house reef. Cherish the quiet morning underwater one last time. Collect your favorite memories of the marine life you've encountered throughout the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon packing, souvenir shopping at the resort boutique, and writing postcards or a travel journal entry. Enjoy a final dip in the lagoon and take photos of the resort to remember it by. Arrange any last-minute transfers or airport logistics with the concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Sunset Dhoni Cruise — book a final sunset cruise (a shorter, more casual version) or simply watch the sunset from the beach with a glass of champagne. Reflect on 12 incredible days in paradise together.

meals.breakfast: Full resort buffet — make the most of it! Try everything you haven't yet and enjoy a long, leisurely final breakfast
meals.lunch: Final resort lunch — a favorite dish from the trip, perhaps the grilled fish or Maldivian curry that won your hearts
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the resort's main restaurant — order your absolute favorite dishes from the trip. Toast to your honeymoon with a bottle of sparkling wine or a signature cocktail.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure transfer timing for the next morning. Pack reef-safe sunscreen, any shells collected, and all souvenirs carefully. Check for any items left in the safe or bathroom. Leave a review for the resort if you enjoyed your stay.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise on the beach. Enjoy a light breakfast before checkout. Take a final walk along the lagoon, breathe in the salt air, and say goodbye to your paradise. Check out and take the speedboat or ferry transfer back to Velana International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Velana International Airport. Arrive with plenty of time for check-in and security. Browse the duty-free shops for last-minute Maldivian souvenirs — local honey, dried tuna, handicrafts, or resort-branded items.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry the memories of 13 magical days in the Maldives — sunsets, bioluminescent waters, coral reefs, and the romance of your honeymoon — home with you.

meals.breakfast: Light checkout breakfast at the resort — croissants, fruit, and coffee before transfer
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café — international options available at Velana International Airport
meals.dinner: On the flight or at a transit airport

day_by_day.notes: Speedboat transfers to the airport typically take 20–40 minutes. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the transfer and check-in. Keep all travel documents, passports, and boarding passes easily accessible. The Maldives charges a departure tax which is usually included in your airline ticket.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Maldives Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: North Malé Atoll, near Hulhumalé lagoon Boutique Stay
hotel.location: North Malé Atoll, near Hulhumalé lagoon

experiences.name: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne
experiences.description: Embark on a traditional Maldivian wooden boat (dhoni) decorated with flowers and candles for a private sunset cruise. Sip champagne while watching the Indian Ocean sky transform into shades of gold and pink. Perfect for honeymooners seeking an intimate and unforgettable romantic experience on the water.
experiences.location: North Malé Atoll, near Hulhumalé lagoon

experiences.name: House Reef Snorkeling Safari with Marine Biologist
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant coral gardens and teeming marine life of a pristine house reef guided by a certified marine biologist. Encounter sea turtles, reef sharks, manta rays, and hundreds of tropical fish species. Snorkeling equipment is provided, and the guide offers fascinating insights into the Maldivian ecosystem throughout the experience.
experiences.location: South Ari Atoll, near Rangali Island

experiences.name: Underwater Spa Treatment
experiences.description: Indulge in a signature couples massage inside a breathtaking glass-walled underwater spa suite surrounded by the turquoise ocean and tropical fish. This ultra-luxurious experience combines therapeutic relaxation with the mesmerizing beauty of the Maldivian sea, making it an iconic and deeply romantic honeymoon memory.
experiences.location: Conrad Maldives Rangali Island, Alif Dhaal Atoll

experiences.name: Maldivian Cooking Class and Beachside Dinner
experiences.description: Learn to prepare authentic Maldivian dishes such as mas huni (tuna and coconut salad), garudhiya fish soup, and coconut-infused curries from a local chef. After the class, enjoy your freshly prepared meal at a candlelit table set directly on the white sand beach under a canopy of stars — a truly magical cultural and culinary experience for couples.

experiences.name: Bioluminescent Night Snorkeling Experience
experiences.description: Slip into the warm, dark waters of the Indian Ocean after sunset to witness the magical phenomenon of bioluminescence — glowing plankton that light up the sea like a constellation of stars beneath the surface. A guided and safe experience with expert instructors, this rare natural wonder is one of the most romantic and awe-inspiring activities available in the Maldives.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and collect luggage. Meet your dedicated resort butler at the arrivals hall for a seamless VIP transfer via private speedboat to your boutique stay in North Malé Atoll near Hulhumalé lagoon. Settle into your overwater or beach villa, enjoy a welcome amenity of fresh tropical fruit, chilled towels, and a glass of sparkling wine prepared by your butler. Take a leisurely orientation stroll around the property and dip into your private plunge pool.
day_by_day.evening: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne — embark on a flower-and-candle-decorated traditional Maldivian dhoni departing from the resort's jetty. Sip premium champagne as the sun melts into the Indian Ocean horizon, creating a breathtaking palette of gold and crimson — the perfect romantic welcome to the Maldives.

meals.breakfast: Enjoyed on the flight or at the airport lounge
meals.lunch: Welcome light bites and tropical refreshments served upon villa arrival, curated by the resort's culinary team
meals.dinner: Intimate beachside dinner for two at the resort's signature overwater restaurant — enjoy freshly caught grilled lobster, saffron-infused seafood bisque, and a curated wine pairing menu under a canopy of stars

day_by_day.notes: Inform the resort in advance of your arrival time so the butler and speedboat transfer are ready. Request rose petal turndown service for your first night as a honeymoon touch. Keep the evening light as jet lag may set in.

day_by_day.morning: Indulge in a leisurely in-villa floating breakfast served on your private deck or pool — think freshly baked pastries, tropical fruit platters, eggs cooked to order, freshly squeezed juices, and barista-crafted coffee. Afterward, enjoy a gentle morning swim in the lagoon directly accessible from your villa, soaking in the serene turquoise waters of Hulhumalé lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: House Reef Snorkeling Safari with Marine Biologist — guided by a certified marine biologist, explore the vibrant coral gardens and teeming marine life of the resort's pristine house reef. Encounter sea turtles, reef sharks, manta rays, and kaleidoscopic tropical fish. Your guide will provide expert narration on the ecosystem, making this both thrilling and educational. All premium snorkeling equipment including prescription masks if needed are provided.
day_by_day.evening: Unwind with sundowner cocktails at the resort's overwater bar, watching the sky transition to deep violet. Dress for a romantic candlelit dinner on a private sandbank — a dedicated table set just for two, surrounded by the gentle sound of lapping waves and illuminated by lanterns and torches.

meals.breakfast: Lavish floating in-villa breakfast — a honeymoon signature experience
meals.lunch: Casual beachside grill lunch at the resort's beach club — freshly grilled mahi-mahi tacos, ceviche, and chilled coconut water served in whole coconuts
meals.dinner: Exclusive private sandbank dinner — a five-course tasting menu featuring Maldivian lobster thermidor, seared yellowfin tuna tataki, and a decadent chocolate lava cake for two with sparkling wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private sandbank dinner at least 24 hours in advance through your butler. Apply reef-safe sunscreen before snorkeling to protect the coral ecosystem. The marine biologist session typically lasts 90 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a peaceful sunrise yoga session on the beach or your villa deck, guided by the resort's resident yoga instructor. The soft morning light over the lagoon creates an impossibly tranquil atmosphere. Follow with a nourishing smoothie bowl and herbal tea at the wellness pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Underwater Spa Treatment — the crown jewel of the trip. Indulge in a signature couples massage inside the resort's breathtaking glass-walled underwater spa suite, surrounded by the mesmerizing blue of the Indian Ocean and schools of tropical fish gliding past. Choose from hot stone massage, aromatherapy, or a Maldivian coconut oil treatment. The session lasts approximately 90 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent Night Snorkeling Experience — slip into the warm dark waters of the Indian Ocean after sunset to witness the magical phenomenon of bioluminescence. Tiny plankton light up the sea in electric blue as you move through the water, creating an otherworldly, deeply romantic experience unique to the Maldives.

meals.breakfast: Wellness breakfast at the resort's garden restaurant — acai bowls, chia pudding, green smoothies, and a selection of organic teas and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Overwater restaurant — pan-seared barramundi with lemongrass coconut broth, prawn tempura, and a chilled rosé from the resort's curated wine cellar
meals.dinner: Post-bioluminescence late dinner at the resort's intimate lounge restaurant — light yet indulgent menu of truffle pasta, sashimi platter, and a shared dessert board with artisanal chocolates and Maldivian sweet treats

day_by_day.notes: The underwater spa is one of the most sought-after experiences — book immediately upon arrival. Bioluminescence is best observed on moonless nights; your butler can confirm optimal timing. Avoid using sunscreen before night snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed morning at your own pace — lounge on your private villa deck, take a dip in your plunge pool, or stroll the resort's white sand beach. Optional: visit the resort's overwater gym for a sunrise workout with panoramic ocean views before a refreshing outdoor shower.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maldivian Cooking Class and Beachside Dinner preparation — spend the afternoon with the resort's executive chef learning to prepare authentic Maldivian dishes: mas huni (tuna and coconut salad), garudhiya fish broth, rihaakuru paste, and freshly baked roshi flatbread. Discover the aromatic spices and traditional techniques that define Maldivian cuisine in a hands-on, intimate class setting on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your culinary labor at a beachside dinner — the dishes you prepared are elegantly plated and served at a private table on the sand, paired with curated cocktails featuring local ingredients like pandan, coconut, and passion fruit. A truly personal and memorable dining experience.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort's main restaurant — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh tropical fruit, and a Maldivian-style coconut pancake stack
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — mezze-style spread of hummus, grilled flatbreads, marinated olives, and chilled gazpacho, with fresh lemonade and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Your personally prepared Maldivian feast served beachside — mas huni, garudhiya soup, grilled reef fish, and coconut-based desserts, paired with premium cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically accommodates couples privately. Inform the chef of any dietary restrictions or allergies in advance. Request a recipe card keepsake to recreate the dishes at home — a beautiful honeymoon memory.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding session through the calm, crystal-clear waters of Hulhumalé lagoon. Your resort guide will lead you through hidden lagoon corners, pointing out starfish, rays, and reef fish visible through the glassy surface. A wonderfully active yet peaceful way to start the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure afternoon — retreat to the resort's infinity pool or private villa pool for a long, languid afternoon of sunbathing, reading, and sipping on handcrafted cocktails delivered by your poolside attendant. Optional: indulge in a solo spa treatment such as a Maldivian herbal body wrap or a deep-cleansing facial at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne (second experience, different route) — this time explore a different stretch of the atoll by dhoni as the sun sets, with a charcuterie and cheese board served alongside premium champagne. Watch for spinner dolphins that frequently accompany boats in the late afternoon.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast delivered to your villa terrace — freshly baked croissants, artisan jams, cold cuts, a fruit bowl, and freshly brewed coffee with steamed coconut milk
meals.lunch: Overwater restaurant — lobster bisque, seared scallops with truffle foam, and a shared seafood tower for two with chilled white Burgundy
meals.dinner: Romantic in-villa dining experience — your butler sets up a private candlelit table on your deck. Menu features surf and turf: grilled Maldivian lobster tail and wagyu beef tenderloin with sides of truffle mashed potato and seasonal vegetables, paired with a fine Bordeaux

day_by_day.notes: Check with the resort about dolphin spotting probability during the dhoni cruise — March is generally an excellent month for sightings. The in-villa dining setup should be requested at least 3 hours in advance through your butler.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion begins with an early morning private speedboat transfer to a remote uninhabited sandbank in the North Malé Atoll. Arrive to find a pristine white sandbar emerging from turquoise waters — completely private. Enjoy a champagne breakfast set up on the sandbank by resort staff who then discreetly depart, leaving you in blissful solitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling around the sandbank's surrounding reef — explore an untouched coral ecosystem teeming with marine life far from any crowds. Your marine equipment is packed in the excursion bag. Afterward, lounge on the sandbank on provided sunbeds with a parasol, refreshments, and a gourmet picnic hamper.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by private speedboat in time for sunset. Freshen up and head to the overwater bar for signature cocktails before a leisurely dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on a private uninhabited sandbank — smoked salmon bagels, fresh fruit skewers, artisan pastries, and Moët & Chandon
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic hamper on the sandbank — truffle sandwiches, lobster rolls, chilled prawns, fresh tropical fruit, brownies, and sparkling water with infused fruit
meals.dinner: Resort's signature fine dining restaurant — seven-course chef's tasting menu featuring Maldivian-inspired contemporary cuisine: tuna tartare, coconut-cured snapper, wagyu short rib, and a passion fruit soufflé, with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: This is a full-day excursion — pack reef-safe sunscreen, hats, sunglasses, and light cover-ups. The resort will prepare the sandbank setup in advance. Confirm weather conditions the evening before with your butler. March weather is typically ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and rejuvenation day. Sleep in and enjoy a late in-villa breakfast at your leisure. Spend the morning on your private deck, reading, journaling, or simply listening to the ocean. Optional gentle beach walk along the resort's shore collecting shells and enjoying the morning calm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Couples spa journey at the resort spa — begin with a shared steam and sauna session, followed by a traditional Maldivian Boraboraa ritual (coconut oil massage with warm volcanic stones), and conclude with a refreshing aloe vera after-sun treatment. The full journey lasts approximately 3 hours and is designed specifically for couples.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent Night Snorkeling Experience (if not done on Day 3, or repeat for a different location) — alternatively, enjoy a private stargazing experience on the beach with a resort astronomer who uses a high-powered telescope to identify constellations and planets, paired with hot cocoa and desserts under the Maldivian sky.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late in-villa breakfast — eggs your way, smoked salmon, avocado toast on sourdough, fresh juices, and a pot of specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Casual beach club lunch — wood-fired pizza with local seafood toppings, burrata salad with heirloom tomatoes, and fresh watermelon juice
meals.dinner: Overwater restaurant — relaxed yet elegant dinner of pan-roasted sea bass, lobster ravioli, and a shared dessert platter of crème brûlée, dark chocolate mousse, and Maldivian coconut ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally paced as a rest and wellness day — the halfway point of the trip. Encourage yourselves to fully disconnect from devices and immerse in the present moment. The couples spa journey should be booked 24 hours ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided fishing excursion on a traditional Maldivian dhoni — try your hand at traditional line fishing in the style locals have practiced for centuries. The crew will assist you in catching reef fish in the calm morning waters of the atoll. A refreshing and authentic cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: House Reef Snorkeling Safari (second session, different reef section) — return to the house reef with your marine biologist guide to explore a different section of the coral garden, focusing on nocturnal creatures resting during the day such as moray eels, sleeping sharks, and octopus. Snorkel for 90 minutes before returning to the resort for a relaxed afternoon by the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise — enjoy a third dhoni experience, this time with a focus on the outer atoll channels where larger pelagic fish and occasional whale sharks are spotted. Sip sundowner cocktails as your crew navigates the golden-lit waters.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-excursion breakfast at the resort restaurant — hearty full English breakfast with local additions of coconut roshi and Maldivian short eats (bajiya fish cakes and gulha fish balls)
meals.lunch: Cook your catch — the resort's chef prepares your morning-caught fish any style you prefer: grilled whole with garlic butter, in a fragrant curry, or as a ceviche. Served at the beachside grill with salads and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Romantic overwater restaurant dinner — tasting menu with ocean-to-table philosophy: reef fish carpaccio, prawn bisque, grilled catch of the day with saffron risotto, and a vanilla panna cotta with mango coulis

day_by_day.notes: The fishing excursion departs early (typically 6:00–6:30 AM) — confirm departure time with your butler the evening before. Catch-and-release is practiced for larger species. The cook-your-catch lunch is a truly special personalized experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided snorkeling excursion by speedboat to a renowned snorkeling site in the North Malé Atoll — visit a famous manta ray cleaning station or a coral pinnacle known for large schools of fish, eagle rays, and nurse sharks resting on the sandy bottom. Your marine biologist guide accompanies you for expert commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for a leisurely lunch, followed by an afternoon of pure indulgence — arrange for a private beach butler setup with a cabana, personalized cocktail menu, chilled towels, and a selection of premium snacks. Read, nap, or simply gaze at the horizon in absolute luxury.
day_by_day.evening: Underwater Spa Treatment (evening session if available) — some resorts offer evening underwater spa sessions where the illuminated ocean creates a magical blue glow around the glass walls. Alternatively, enjoy a private in-villa spa treatment with a therapist setting up in your villa for a candlelit couples massage.

meals.breakfast: Overwater restaurant breakfast buffet — an extensive spread of fresh tropical fruits, cold cuts, cheeses, pastries, live cooking stations for eggs and pancakes, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Beachside light lunch — sushi and sashimi platter, edamame, miso soup, and Japanese-inspired cocktails with yuzu and sake, enjoyed under your private beach cabana
meals.dinner: Special honeymoon dinner arranged by the resort — a fully personalized menu designed by the executive chef based on your preferences, served at the most coveted table in the restaurant with complimentary honeymoon cake and a bottle of vintage champagne

day_by_day.notes: Day 9 marks the final third of the trip — a great time to reflect on highlights and consider any repeat experiences you'd like to book again before departure. Speak to your butler about any special anniversary or honeymoon surprises you'd like arranged.

day_by_day.morning: Private windsurfing or kitesurfing lesson with the resort's water sports instructor — March brings consistent trade winds to the Maldives, making it ideal for wind sports. Alternatively, enjoy a private sailing lesson on a small catamaran in the lagoon. A fun, active, and exhilarating way to experience the atoll from a new perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maldivian Cultural Experience — arrange a guided visit to a nearby local island (accessible by short speedboat transfer) to experience authentic Maldivian village life. Visit the local mosque, watch traditional bodu beru drumming, browse local craft markets, and interact with friendly islanders. A meaningful contrast to resort life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for sunset cocktails at the overwater bar, followed by a relaxed dinner. Tonight, celebrate the second-to-last full week of the trip with a special bottle of vintage wine selected by the resort sommelier.

meals.breakfast: In-villa continental breakfast — freshly baked bread, premium cold cuts, organic honey, tropical preserves, and barista coffee with your choice of milk
meals.lunch: Local island experience — taste authentic Maldivian street food: hedhikaa short eats, fresh coconut, and sweet bondi (local doughnuts), followed by a refreshing drink at a local café
meals.dinner: Resort's overwater restaurant — Mediterranean-inspired menu of burrata with heirloom tomatoes, grilled branzino with lemon caper butter, handmade tagliatelle with seafood ragù, and a tiramisu for two with dessert wine

day_by_day.notes: The local island visit offers a respectful and enriching cultural immersion — dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) when visiting the mosque and village areas. Purchase locally made souvenirs to support the community. Confirm speedboat transfer timing with your butler.

day_by_day.morning: Guided sunrise snorkeling session — join the marine biologist for a special early morning snorkel on the house reef when the ocean is at its most calm and the light creates extraordinary visibility. Witness nocturnal creatures returning to their hiding spots and diurnal fish beginning their morning feeding. A truly magical and rarely experienced perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full spa afternoon — dedicate the entire afternoon to wellness. Begin with a Maldivian Jangli herbal steam treatment, followed by a full-body exfoliation using coconut and sea salt scrub, then a 90-minute deep tissue massage, and conclude with a nourishing hair and scalp treatment. Emerge completely renewed.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent Night Snorkeling Experience — if not yet experienced, tonight is the perfect opportunity. Alternatively, arrange a private beach bonfire with the resort team — roast marshmallows, sip spiced rum cocktails, and share stories by firelight on your private stretch of beach, with a sky full of stars overhead.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-snorkel breakfast — fresh fruit, yogurt parfait, granola, and green tea served at the wellness pavilion or your villa
meals.lunch: Post-spa nourishment lunch — detox-focused menu of Buddha bowls, quinoa salads, cold-pressed juices, and herbal infusions at the resort's health-conscious café
meals.dinner: Romantic beachside bonfire dinner — an intimate barbecue setup on the beach with premium cuts of wagyu beef, whole grilled lobster, seasonal vegetables, and artisanal bread, with a curated selection of fine wines and cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Day 11 is a wonderful day to fully surrender to relaxation and sensory experiences. The bonfire dinner must be arranged in advance with your butler. Bring a light wrap for the evening as the breeze can be refreshing after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day snorkeling adventure — a longer guided snorkeling safari by speedboat to two or three of the North Malé Atoll's best snorkeling sites, including a coral garden, a channel known for hammerhead sharks (seasonal), and a lagoon frequented by sea turtles. Pack your underwater camera for this memorable final underwater journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort and spend the afternoon souvenir shopping at the resort boutique for premium Maldivian crafts, lacquerware, and keepsakes. Then enjoy a final long swim in the lagoon and a sunset photography walk along the beach — capture the colors, textures, and beauty of this extraordinary place to take home with you.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner — the resort's chef prepares a bespoke eight-course tasting menu celebrating the finest ingredients of the Indian Ocean and Maldivian culinary heritage. Paired with a premium wine flight selected by the sommelier. The resort presents you with a honeymoon memento — a framed photo from your trip or a personalized keepsake.

meals.breakfast: Festive à la carte breakfast at the restaurant — eggs royale with caviar, smoked salmon, champagne mimosas, and a full tropical fruit display
meals.lunch: Casual farewell beach lunch — grilled reef fish tacos, ceviche, guacamole, and fresh coconut water, relaxed and unhurried
meals.dinner: Eight-course farewell tasting menu at the resort's finest restaurant — a culinary journey through Maldivian flavors elevated with French technique, champagne toast included, honeymoon cake presented by the chef

day_by_day.notes: Ask the resort's photographer to capture this final evening — many luxury resorts offer complimentary or bookable photography sessions. Confirm checkout time and departure transfer arrangements with your butler this evening to ensure a stress-free final morning.
